commits.message:
docs(openspec): propose version history snapshots

OpenSpec change add-version-snapshots for Roadmap #19: a new
plugin-snapshots package with host-injected async storage, plus the
electron-demo reference implementation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(snapshots): add version history plugin with host-injected storage

New @floatboat/nexus-plugin-snapshots package: capture/list/restore/
delete document snapshots scoped per host-supplied document key, with
FNV-1a content de-duplication, retention pruning, idle auto-capture,
and a safe restore flow (safety snapshot + single undoable setDocument).

Persistence is host-injected via an async SnapshotStore; the default is
an in-memory store and nothing touches localStorage or the filesystem
implicitly. Store failures degrade to no-ops instead of breaking the
editor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(electron): add snapshots reference implementation

File-backed SnapshotStore over IPC persisting snapshots inside the
vault at .nexus/snapshots/<sha1(documentKey)>/ as content .md plus
metadata .json sidecars (append-only, no shared index). Dot-directory
writes no longer re-seed the link index via the vault watcher.

Renderer: snapshots panel (list / capture / restore-with-confirm /
delete) behind a toolbar toggle, capture-on-save, and per-file history
keyed by the active file path. Falls back to the in-memory store when
the preload bridge is absent (unit tests, browser hosts).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: register snapshots plugin, scope, and roadmap status

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(snapshots): add lazy age-based snapshot expiry

Hosts can bound how long snapshots live via maxAgeMs, complementing the
maxSnapshots count cap. Expiry is swept lazily — after every capture and
via an explicit prune() the demo calls at startup — rather than on a
background timer, matching how Obsidian expires its snapshots. The demo
configures 30-day expiry.

The engine's capture invokes the sweep body directly: routing it through
the public queued prune() would deadlock against the in-flight capture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+## Context
+
+Roadmap #19 asks for "Version history / snapshots" with package ownership `core` + host storage. Investigation shows the plugin surface (`NexusPlugin.commands`, `EditorAPI.setDocument`, `on`/`off` events) already covers every hook this feature needs, and the `add-search-query-history` change established the host-injected storage precedent inside a plugin package. Building this as a plugin package therefore matches the repo's actual pattern better than extending `core`, and keeps the capability opt-in with zero cost for hosts that don't enable it.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+- Goals:
+  - Pure, deterministic snapshot engine (hash de-dup, retention) that is fully unit-testable without a DOM.
+  - Async host-injected `SnapshotStore` so the electron-demo can persist snapshots as files over IPC.
+  - Restore flow that is safe by construction: safety snapshot first, then an undoable `setDocument`.
+  - Electron-demo reference implementation: file-backed store + snapshots panel.
+- Non-Goals: diff UI, cloud sync, core API changes, React/Vue binding changes.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Decision 1: New plugin package, no core changes.**
+  Alternatives considered: adding a snapshot API to `core`'s `EditorAPI`. Rejected — every operation (read document, replace document, observe changes, register commands) is already public; a `core` change would widen the stable API surface for a feature most hosts may not enable. `NexusPlugin.commands` gives the command-palette integration for free.
+
+- **Decision 2: Async `SnapshotStore` interface.**
+  `list` / `load` / `save` / `remove` / `clear` all return promises. The search-history storage is synchronous (`getItem`/`setItem`), which fits `localStorage` but cannot represent file or IPC backends — the exact backends Roadmap #19 targets. The plugin ships `createMemorySnapshotStore()` for tests and headless hosts.
+
+- **Decision 3: Content-hash de-duplication against the newest snapshot.**
+  Capture hashes the document (FNV-1a, no dependency) and skips the write when it matches the newest snapshot for the same document key. This makes idle auto-capture cheap and keeps "restore then capture" from bouncing. Only the newest snapshot is compared — older duplicates are left alone, so a user returning to an earlier state still gets a fresh, correctly-ordered snapshot.
+
+- **Decision 4: Safety snapshot before restore.**
+  `restore()` first captures the current buffer (labelled `Before restore …`) so an accidental restore is itself recoverable; the restore then goes through `setDocument`, which dispatches a single transaction and therefore remains one `undo()` step. The safety capture runs through the normal de-dup path, so it is skipped when the buffer already matches the restore target or the newest snapshot (e.g. an idle auto-capture that just recorded the same content) — the content is preserved either way. The restore's own `setDocument` also suppresses the pending idle auto-capture, so a restore never grows a duplicate of the restored content.
+
+- **Decision 5: Per-document keying via `getDocumentKey()`.**
+  The host tells the plugin which document is active (electron-demo: the absolute file path, falling back to a fixed "untitled" key). Snapshots for different files never interleave, and switching files re-keys all subsequent operations. A fixed string also works for single-document hosts.
+
+- **Decision 6: Idle-based auto-capture.**
+  When `autoCapture.intervalMs` is set, each `change` event (re)starts an idle timer; when the user pauses for the interval, one snapshot is taken. De-dup (Decision 3) guarantees no-op captures stay free. There is deliberately no wall-clock periodic mode: it snapshots unchanged documents and adds timer complexity for no user benefit.
+
+- **Decision 7: Electron-demo stores snapshots inside the vault at `.nexus/snapshots/<document-hash>/`.**
+  Snapshots travel with the vault (portable, vault-scoped) instead of living in Electron's `userData`. The vault tree walker skips dot-directories, so the folder stays invisible in the file panel and out of the link index. Each snapshot is a `<id>.md` content file plus a `<id>.json` metadata sidecar — append-only, no shared index file that could corrupt concurrent writes.
+
+- **Decision 8: Retention is count-based plus optional lazy age-based expiry.**
+  `maxSnapshots` bounds how many versions accumulate; `maxAgeMs` (e.g. 30 days in the demo) bounds how long they live. Expiry is swept lazily — after every capture and via an explicit `prune()` the demo calls at startup — instead of on a background timer. Timers are unreliable in long-lived editor sessions, the storage is host-owned, and sweeping on access is the same model Obsidian uses. The engine's internal sweep must not re-enter its own operation queue (a queued public `prune` called from an in-flight queued `capture` deadlocks), so `capture` invokes the sweep body directly.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- Async store operations race with rapid capture/restore clicks → the plugin serializes engine operations on a per-plugin promise queue; UI-triggered calls simply queue up.
+- Retention pruning deletes files the host might still hold ids for → `remove` of a missing id is a no-op, `load` of a missing id resolves `null`, and `restore(null)` is a no-op.
+- Large documents make full-text snapshots heavy → out of scope to delta-encode; the retention cap bounds total size, and de-dup prevents idle growth.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+Purely additive. Hosts that don't install the plugin see no change. No data migration.
+
+## Open Questions
+
+- Should a future change add a shared storage-adapter contract in `core` for all plugins (search history, snapshots, …)? Deferred — Roadmap #23 (cloud storage interface) is the right place to generalize.

+# Change: Add Version History / Snapshots
+
+## Why
+
+Roadmap #19 ("Version history / snapshots") calls for point-in-time document snapshots with host-injected storage, so users can recover earlier versions of a note without any cloud dependency. This change delivers a new `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-snapshots` package plus the electron-demo reference implementation called out in the roadmap ("electron-demo lands the reference impl first").
+
+## What Changes
+
+- Add a new package `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-snapshots` exposing `createSnapshotsPlugin()`.
+- Capture full-document snapshots manually (named editor command) and automatically (idle-based auto-capture after edits, opt-in).
+- De-duplicate consecutive snapshots by content hash — an unchanged document never produces a new snapshot.
+- Scope snapshots per document via a host-supplied `getDocumentKey()` (e.g. active file path); each key has an independent snapshot list.
+- Enforce a configurable `maxSnapshots` retention cap per document, dropping the oldest snapshots first.
+- Restore a snapshot through `EditorAPI.setDocument()` so the restore is itself undoable; automatically capture a safety snapshot of the current content before restoring.
+- Support host-injected async storage (`SnapshotStore`) for persistence — the plugin ships an in-memory store and never touches `localStorage` or the filesystem implicitly.
+- Treat unavailable storage, thrown store operations, and missing snapshot ids as recoverable.
+- Electron demo: file-backed `SnapshotStore` over IPC (stored inside the vault under `.nexus/snapshots/`), a snapshots panel (list / capture / restore / delete), and capture-on-save.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- No diff / side-by-side comparison UI in this PR (list + restore only).
+- No changes to `packages/core` — the plugin builds on the existing public `EditorAPI`.
+- No cloud sync of snapshots; storage backend is the host's responsibility.
+- No snapshot branching, naming beyond a single label, or per-range restore.
+- No changes to the React / Vue bindings.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Affected specs: `plugins`
+- Affected code:
+  - `packages/plugin-snapshots/` (new package)
+  - `apps/electron-demo/electron/main.ts` (snapshot IPC handlers)
+  - `apps/electron-demo/electron/preload.ts` (snapshot bridge)
+  - `apps/electron-demo/src/renderer/` (snapshots panel, shell + app wiring)
+  - `vitest.config.ts` (package alias)
+  - `README.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md` (status/docs)
+- Affected roadmap: reference implementation for Roadmap #19.

+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Version Snapshots Scope
+
+`@floatboat/nexus-plugin-snapshots` SHALL provide document version history as the reference implementation of Roadmap #19 ("Version history / snapshots"). This change SHALL cover full-document snapshot capture, per-document listing, restore, deletion, and retention. Diff / comparison UI, cloud sync, and changes to `packages/core` SHALL remain follow-up work outside this PR.
+
+#### Scenario: Plugin-based first stage
+- **WHEN** a host adds `createSnapshotsPlugin()` to `createEditor({ plugins })`
+- **THEN** the host SHALL be able to capture, list, restore, and delete full-document snapshots
+- **AND** `packages/core` public API SHALL remain unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: Diff UI remains a follow-up
+- **WHEN** a reviewer evaluates this change against Roadmap #19
+- **THEN** the proposal SHALL identify diff / comparison UI and cloud sync as non-goals
+- **AND** those behaviors SHALL NOT be required for this PR to be complete
+
+### Requirement: Opt-In Backward Compatibility
+
+Version snapshots SHALL be opt-in. Hosts that do not install the plugin SHALL see no change in editor behavior, and no snapshot data SHALL be written anywhere by default.
+
+#### Scenario: No plugin, no snapshots
+- **WHEN** a host creates an editor without `createSnapshotsPlugin()`
+- **THEN** no snapshot storage SHALL be read or written
+- **AND** editor behavior SHALL be unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: Default in-memory storage
+- **WHEN** a host creates `createSnapshotsPlugin()` without a `store`
+- **THEN** snapshots SHALL be kept in memory only
+- **AND** the plugin SHALL NOT write to global `localStorage`, the filesystem, or any other implicit persistence
+
+### Requirement: Host-Injected Persistence
+
+The plugin SHALL support host-injected async storage via a `SnapshotStore` interface (`list` / `load` / `save` / `remove` / `clear`). Persistent storage must be provided explicitly by the host.
+
+#### Scenario: Host store persists snapshots
+- **GIVEN** the host provides a `SnapshotStore`
+- **WHEN** a snapshot is captured
+- **THEN** the plugin SHALL write the snapshot content and metadata (id, createdAt, label) through the store under the current document key
+
+#### Scenario: Snapshot survives reload
+- **GIVEN** a host store that persists data across editor instances
+- **WHEN** a snapshot was captured by a previous editor instance
+- **THEN** a new plugin instance bound to the same store and document key SHALL list and restore that snapshot
+
+### Requirement: Snapshot Capture Rules
+
+Capture SHALL record the current document with an optional trimmed label. Consecutive snapshots with identical content SHALL be de-duplicated by content hash: if the newest snapshot for the document has the same content, capture SHALL be a no-op. Snapshots SHALL be scoped per document key supplied by the host's `getDocumentKey()`.
+
+#### Scenario: Manual capture via command
+- **GIVEN** the plugin is attached to an editor
+- **WHEN** the host runs the `snapshots.capture` editor command
+- **THEN** a snapshot of the current document SHALL be recorded
+
+#### Scenario: Identical content is not re-captured
+- **GIVEN** a snapshot of the current document already exists as the newest entry
+- **WHEN** capture runs again without any document change
+- **THEN** no new snapshot SHALL be created
+
+#### Scenario: Changed content produces a new snapshot
+- **GIVEN** the newest snapshot contains "alpha"
+- **WHEN** the document changes to "alpha beta" and capture runs
+- **THEN** a new snapshot SHALL be created and listed as the newest entry
+
+#### Scenario: Labels are trimmed and blank labels are dropped
+- **WHEN** capture is called with the label `"  before refactor  "`
+- **THEN** the stored label SHALL be `"before refactor"`
+- **WHEN** capture is called with a whitespace-only label
+- **THEN** the snapshot SHALL be stored with no label
+
+#### Scenario: Document keys isolate snapshot lists
+- **GIVEN** snapshots exist for document key "a.md"
+- **WHEN** the host's `getDocumentKey()` returns "b.md"
+- **THEN** listing SHALL return only snapshots for "b.md"
+- **AND** capturing SHALL write under "b.md"
+
+#### Scenario: Idle auto-capture
+- **GIVEN** `autoCapture.intervalMs` is configured
+- **WHEN** the document changes and then remains idle for the interval
+- **THEN** exactly one snapshot SHALL be captured
+- **AND** continued typing SHALL reset the idle timer before it fires
+
+### Requirement: Snapshot Retention
+
+Each document key SHALL retain at most `maxSnapshots` snapshots (default 50). When the cap is exceeded, the oldest snapshots SHALL be removed first. When `maxAgeMs` is configured, snapshots older than that age SHALL be pruned lazily — on capture and when the host calls `prune()` — rather than by a background timer.
+
+#### Scenario: Oldest snapshots are dropped
+- **GIVEN** `maxSnapshots` is `2`
+- **WHEN** three snapshots with different content are captured in order
+- **THEN** only the two newest snapshots SHALL remain listed
+
+#### Scenario: Expired snapshots are pruned on capture
+- **GIVEN** `maxAgeMs` is configured and a snapshot older than that age exists
+- **WHEN** a new snapshot is captured
+- **THEN** the expired snapshot SHALL be removed
+
+#### Scenario: Startup sweep without a new capture
+- **GIVEN** `maxAgeMs` is configured and only expired snapshots exist
+- **WHEN** the host calls `prune()` (e.g. at app startup)
+- **THEN** the expired snapshots SHALL be removed without capturing anything new
+
+### Requirement: Safe Restore
+
+Restore SHALL replace the editor document through `EditorAPI.setDocument()` so the restore itself is undoable. Before replacing the document, the plugin SHALL capture a safety snapshot of the current content — skipped when the current content is already preserved (identical to the restore target, or identical to the newest snapshot via de-duplication). Restoring a missing or deleted snapshot id SHALL be a no-op.
+
+#### Scenario: Restore replaces the document
+- **GIVEN** a snapshot with content "alpha" and a current document "beta"
+- **WHEN** the snapshot is restored
+- **THEN** the editor document SHALL become "alpha"
+
+#### Scenario: Safety snapshot before restore
+- **GIVEN** a snapshot with content "alpha" and a current document "beta"
+- **WHEN** the snapshot is restored
+- **THEN** a new snapshot containing "beta" SHALL exist
+- **AND** restoring that safety snapshot SHALL bring back "beta"
+
+#### Scenario: No safety snapshot when content matches
+- **GIVEN** the current document is identical to the snapshot being restored
+- **WHEN** restore runs
+- **THEN** no additional snapshot SHALL be created
+
+#### Scenario: Missing snapshot id is a no-op
+- **WHEN** restore is called with an id that does not exist in the store
+- **THEN** the editor document SHALL be unchanged
+- **AND** no error SHALL be thrown
+
+### Requirement: Storage Failure Resilience
+
+The plugin SHALL treat unavailable storage, thrown store operations, and missing snapshot ids as recoverable conditions. These failures SHALL NOT crash the editor or leave the plugin in a state where later operations fail.
+
+#### Scenario: Store save throws
+- **GIVEN** the host store rejects on `save`
+- **WHEN** capture runs
+- **THEN** the editor SHALL NOT throw
+- **AND** subsequent captures against a healthy store SHALL still succeed
+
+#### Scenario: Store list throws
+- **GIVEN** the host store rejects on `list`
+- **WHEN** the host lists snapshots
+- **THEN** the call SHALL resolve with an empty list
+- **AND** the editor SHALL continue to operate normally
+
+### Requirement: Electron Demo Reference Implementation
+
+The electron-demo SHALL provide the reference implementation of Roadmap #19: a file-backed `SnapshotStore` exposed over IPC, a snapshots panel for the active file, and capture-on-save. Snapshots SHALL be stored inside the vault under `.nexus/snapshots/`, and the vault file tree SHALL exclude dot-directories so snapshot storage stays invisible.
+
+#### Scenario: Snapshots persist on disk
+- **GIVEN** a vault is open in the electron-demo
+- **WHEN** the user captures a snapshot of the active file
+- **THEN** the snapshot content and metadata SHALL be written under `<vault>/.nexus/snapshots/`
+- **AND** reopening the vault SHALL list the snapshot again
+
+#### Scenario: Snapshot storage is invisible in the vault tree
+- **WHEN** snapshot files exist under `<vault>/.nexus/snapshots/`
+- **THEN** the vault panel tree SHALL NOT show `.nexus` or its contents
+- **AND** the link index SHALL NOT index snapshot files
+
+#### Scenario: Panel lists, restores, and deletes
+- **GIVEN** the snapshots panel is open for the active file
+- **WHEN** the user selects a snapshot and confirms restore
+- **THEN** the editor document SHALL be replaced with the snapshot content
+- **WHEN** the user deletes a snapshot
+- **THEN** it SHALL disappear from the list and from disk
+
+#### Scenario: Capture on save
+- **WHEN** the user saves the active file to the vault
+- **THEN** a snapshot SHALL be captured unless the content is unchanged since the newest snapshot

+# @floatboat/nexus-plugin-snapshots
+
+Version history for Nexus-Editor: capture point-in-time snapshots of the current document, list them per file, and restore any of them — with host-injected persistence and no implicit `localStorage` / filesystem writes.
+
+Reference implementation of [Roadmap #19](../../docs/ROADMAP.md) ("Version history / snapshots"); see `openspec/changes/add-version-snapshots` for the spec.
+
+## Usage
+
+```ts
+import { createEditor } from "@floatboat/nexus-core";
+import {
+  attachSnapshotsPlugin,
+  createSnapshotsPlugin
+} from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-snapshots";
+
+const snapshots = createSnapshotsPlugin({
+  // Optional — defaults to an in-memory store:
+  store: mySnapshotStore,
+  // Snapshots are scoped per key (e.g. the active file path):
+  getDocumentKey: () => activeFilePath ?? "untitled",
+  maxSnapshots: 50,
+  // Optional age-based expiry — pruned on capture and via prune():
+  maxAgeMs: 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
+  autoCapture: { intervalMs: 30_000 } // one snapshot after 30s idle
+});
+
+const editor = createEditor({ container, plugins: [snapshots] });
+attachSnapshotsPlugin(snapshots, editor);
+
+await snapshots.capture("First draft");   // manual capture
+const list = await snapshots.list();       // newest first
+await snapshots.restore(list[0].id);       // safe + undoable
+await snapshots.remove(list[0].id);
+```
+
+A manual capture is also registered as the editor command `snapshots.capture` (label "Snapshots: Take snapshot"), so command palettes can trigger it via `editor.runCommand("snapshots.capture")`.
+
+## Behavior
+
+- **De-duplication** — capturing content identical to the newest snapshot is a no-op (`capture()` resolves `null`). Idle auto-capture therefore never grows the history of an unchanged document.
+- **Safe restore** — before replacing the document, a safety snapshot of the current buffer (label `"Before restore"`) is taken unless the content is already preserved. The restore itself is a single `setDocument` transaction, so one `undo()` reverts it (with `plugin-history` installed).
+- **Retention** — each document key keeps at most `maxSnapshots` entries (default 50); the oldest drop first. With `maxAgeMs` set, snapshots older than that are also pruned — lazily, on capture and when the host calls `prune()` (e.g. at app startup), never on a background timer.
+- **Resilience** — a rejecting store never breaks the editor: failed saves resolve `null`, failed lists resolve `[]`, missing ids are no-ops.
+
+## Persistence (`SnapshotStore`)
+
+Storage is host-injected and fully async, so file / IPC / network backends are representable:
+
+```ts
+interface SnapshotStore {
+  list(documentKey: string): Promise<SnapshotMeta[]>;
+  load(documentKey: string, id: string): Promise<string | null>;
+  save(documentKey: string, snapshot: Snapshot): Promise<void>;
+  remove(documentKey: string, id: string): Promise<void>; // missing id must not throw
+  clear(documentKey: string): Promise<void>;
+}
+```
+
+The default `createMemorySnapshotStore()` keeps everything in memory — persistence only happens when the host explicitly provides a store. The electron-demo (`apps/electron-demo`) ships a file-backed store over IPC that writes snapshots into the vault under `.nexus/snapshots/`.
+
+## API
+
+| Export | Description |
+|---|---|
+| `createSnapshotsPlugin(options?)` | Plugin factory (dual shape: `NexusPlugin` + API handle) |
+| `attachSnapshotsPlugin(plugin, editor)` | Bind to an editor (required for capture / restore / auto-capture) |
+| `SNAPSHOTS_CAPTURE_COMMAND` | Editor command id for manual capture |
+| `createMemorySnapshotStore()` | In-memory `SnapshotStore` (default) |
+| `SnapshotEngine` | DOM-free snapshot bookkeeping (de-dup, retention) for custom integrations |
+| `hashContent(content)` | FNV-1a content hash used for de-duplication |
